source_text:
κελεύων ἀποθέσθαι οὐ τὰ βιωτικά, ἀλλὰ τὰ τούτοις κακῶς χρώμενα· ταῦτα
δὲ ἦν τὰ τῆς ψυχῆς ἀρρωστήματα καὶ πάθη. ὁ τούτων πλοῦτος παρὼν μὲν ἅπασι θανατηφόρος, ἀπολόμενος δὲ σωτήριος· οὗ δεῖ καθαρεύουσαν. τουτέστι πτωχεύουσαν καὶ γυμνήν. τὴν ψυχὴν παρασχόμενον οὕτως ἤδη τοῦ σωτῆρος ἀκοῦσαι λέγοντος· »δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.« ὁδὸς γὰρ αὐτὸς ἤδη τῷ καθαρῷ τὴν καρδίαν γίνεται, εἰς δὲ ἀκάθαρτον ψυχὴν θεοῦ χάρις οὐ παραδύεται· ἀκάθαρτος δὲ ἡ πλουτοῦσα τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν καὶ ὠδίνουσα πολλοῖς ἔρωσι καὶ κοσμικοῖς.
thought_title: The wealth of passions is deadly; the soul must be cleansed to follow Christ
orientation: Clement is explaining what Jesus meant by commanding the rich man to sell his possessions: the things to be cast off are not outward goods but the soul's passions, and only a soul cleansed of them can follow Christ.
pass_a_gloss: He commands to put away not the things of life, but the things that use these badly; these were the sicknesses and passions of the soul. The wealth of these, when present, is deadly to all, but when destroyed, it brings salvation; of this wealth one must provide a soul that is pure, that is, poor and naked. Having provided such a soul, one is then able to hear the Savior saying: "Come, follow me." For he himself now becomes the way for the one pure in heart, but into an unclean soul the grace of God does not slip in; unclean is the soul that is rich in desires and in labor with many worldly loves.

choices.why: Keeps the literal sense of outward, life-related goods, matching Clement's contrast with the soul's passions.
Literal medical metaphor for the soul's diseased state, which Clement uses to describe passions.
Preserves the passive aorist participle's force: the wealth of passions being destroyed, not destroying itself.
Captures the verb's sense of entering secretly or by stealth, fitting the image of grace entering a soul.
Keeps the birth-pang metaphor for the soul's painful production of many loves.

pass_b_english: He commands us to put away, not the things of life, but the things that are used badly. These are the sicknesses and passions of the soul. The wealth of these, when present, is deadly to everyone; when destroyed, it brings salvation. A person must present his soul pure from this wealth—that is, poor and naked—and only then can he hear the Savior say, “Come, follow me” (Mark 10:21). For the way itself now becomes the heart of the one who is pure, but the grace of God does not slip into an unclean soul. And the soul that is unclean is the one rich in desires, tormented by many worldly loves.

problems.why: The quoted words “Come, follow me” are from Mark 10:21, not Matthew 19:21.

problems.quote: in labor with many worldly loves
the things that use them badly
problems.why: Greek says the things are used badly; English makes the things the agents that use life badly.
problems.fix: the things that are used badly
problems.ruling: τὰ τούτοις κακῶς χρώμενα: neuter passive/ middle, 'things used badly by them,' not active agents.

problems.quote: the Lord himself now becomes the way
problems.source_quote: ὁδὸς γὰρ αὐτὸς ἤδη τῷ καθαρῷ τὴν καρδίαν γίνεται
problems.why: Greek says the way itself becomes the heart of the pure one; English adds “the Lord himself” and changes the relationship.
problems.fix: the way itself already becomes the heart of the pure one
problems.ruling: αὐτὸς refers back to σωτῆρος, but 'way becomes for the pure in heart' misrendered; 'heart' is dative of respect, not object.

edits.old: in labor with many worldly loves
the things that use them badly
edits.new: the things that are used badly

edits.old: the Lord himself now becomes the way for the one who is pure in heart
edits.new: the way itself now becomes the heart of the one who is pure

fixed: Wrong scripture reference: source quotes Mark 10:21, not Matthew 19:21.
Mistranslation: ὠδίνουσα means tormented or afflicted, not in labor.
Agency: Greek says the things are used badly, not that they use life badly.
Mistranslation: Greek says the way itself becomes the heart of the pure one, not that the Lord becomes the way for the pure in heart.

last_rejected.quote: For the way itself now becomes the heart of the one who is pure
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁδὸς γὰρ αὐτὸς ἤδη τῷ καθαρῷ τὴν καρδίαν γίνεται
last_rejected.why: Subject and object reversed: Jesus (the way) becomes the way FOR the pure in heart, not 'becomes the heart'.
last_rejected.fix: For he himself becomes the way for the one pure in heart.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek: ὁδὸς … τῷ καθαρῷ τὴν καρδίαν γίνεται = 'the way becomes the heart for the pure'; translation matches.

last_rejected.quote: the grace of God does not slip into
last_rejected.why: παραδύεται means 'sneak in/penetrate', not 'slip into' as accidental; 'enter' or 'penetrate' better.
last_rejected.fix: the grace of God does not enter
last_rejected.ruling: παραδύεται = 'is handed over/given'; 'slip into' is a stylistic nuance, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ὠδίνουσα means 'in labor pangs/giving birth to', not 'tormented by'; she is producing desires, not suffering them.
last_rejected.fix: in labor with many worldly lusts
last_rejected.ruling: ὠδίνουσα with dative = 'in pain because of' many loves; translation 'tormented by' fits.
